title: The 10 Best Cordless Car Polishers
subtitle: Battery-powered dual-action and rotary polishers for waxing and swirl removal without a cord on the paint, ranked from live Amazon data.
intro: A cordless polisher does the same waxing and swirl removal as a corded one without a cord dragging across the paint. We ranked 10 best-sellers on rating, review volume and features (dual-action motion, batteries in the box, a brushless motor and a tool battery platform). Budget kits come with two batteries, a charger and pads; DEWALT and Milwaukee sell pro tools bare for their platforms. They run from about $40 for Avhrit's 6-inch kit to $244 for Milwaukee's M18 FUEL random orbital.

products.name: BATOCA S3 Cordless Car Polisher, DA Orbital Polishing Machine

specs.in_box: 2 batteries, fast charger, pads, tool bag

products.name: SPTA Cordless Car Buffer Polisher, 12V Brushless, 2 Batteries, Variable Speed (LD601US-MIX)

products.name: BATOCA S5 Cordless Mini Car Polisher Buffer, Rotary & Dual Action

products.name: VERVEWAVE Cordless Buffer Polisher for Dewalt 20V Battery, 6-Inch Orbital, 1800-5500 RPM (WT8633)
products.verdict: A third-party brushless orbital polisher that runs on DEWALT 20V batteries, with a 17-piece pad kit and a lock switch. DEWALT doesn't make or warrant it.

products.name: DEWALT 20V MAX XR Cordless Polisher, Rotary, Variable Speed, 7-Inch, Tool Only (DCM849B)

specs.in_box: Backing plate, side and bail handles

products.verdict: A brushless cordless rotary for pros: 800-2,200 rpm with trigger and dial control, a 7-inch plate, side and bail handles, and a rubber overmold that won't mar paint.
products.best_for: Detailers on DEWALT 20V doing correction work.

products.name: Milwaukee 2738-20 M18 FUEL Brushless Cordless 7 inch Variable Speed Polisher, Tool Only
products.verdict: Milwaukee's M18 FUEL 7-inch rotary polisher, promising corded performance on a battery. The listing is thin; check Milwaukee's specs before buying.

products.verdict: A pro-grade 15 mm long-throw random orbital: an 8-speed dial plus variable trigger, electronic feedback that holds speed under load, and a lock-on switch for long sessions.

buyers_guide.q: Is a cordless polisher as good as a corded one?
buyers_guide.a: For waxing and light correction, yes, and there's no cord to drag across the paint. Heavy correction drains batteries fast, so pros often keep a corded polisher for that and a cordless one for touch-ups.
Dual-action polishers are forgiving and won't burn paint, ideal for beginners. Rotaries cut faster but can burn through clear coat if held still.
Throw is how far the pad orbits off-center. 5-8 mm throws are easy to control; 15 mm long-throw polishers like Milwaukee's correct faster on flat panels.

buyers_guide.q: How long do the batteries last?
buyers_guide.a: Budget kits run about 20-40 minutes per 2.0Ah battery, so two batteries cover a waxing session. Tool-platform batteries (4-6Ah) last longer.
Use cutting pads with compound for swirls, polishing pads with polish to refine, and finishing pads for wax. Match pad size to the backing plate.
